section_summary.extract_value: This section, describing Study X, outlines the hypothesis that higher divergent thinking scores (measured by ATTA) would correlate with greater attentional flexibility (smaller RT oddball effect) and increased cognitive control (larger N2 oddball effect). The findings supported these predictions, showing significant negative correlations between total divergent thinking and RT oddball effect (r = -.64), and between total divergent thinking and N2 oddball effect (r = -.67). Specific correlations for fluency and originality were also reported, while no significant correlation was found with the P3b oddball effect.
